title: He cried over the son who betrayed him.
paragraphs: He cried over the son who betrayed him.
Because this is not just a story about a fallen prince.
And if you look closely enough—
you might see yourself in Absalom.
you might hear your Father’s voice in David’s cry.
He stole hearts behind closed gates (2 Samuel 15:6).
He didn’t look like a villain.
“In all Israel there was no one so much to be praised for his handsome appearance as Absalom…” (2 Samuel 14:25)
This is where it gets uncomfortable.
Because some of us know how to perform righteousness…
We wear the image of a son—
but live like we have no Father.
Absalom rode into battle full of confidence.
And then comes the moment no one prepares for.

“O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! Would I had died instead of you…”
(2 Samuel 18:33)
That is a father’s heart breaking open.
David loved a son who rejected him.
And that’s where this story shifts from history…
Because David’s words carry a longing he could not fulfill:
“Would I had died instead of you.”
He wanted to take his son’s place.
That’s the limit of even the greatest human love.
And this is where the Gospel explodes into the story.
You are not just reading about Absalom.
“All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned—every one—to his own way…” (Isaiah 53:6)
A heart turned away from God.
But the verse doesn’t end there.
“…and the LORD has laid on Him the iniquity of us all.”
Where Absalom hung helpless in a tree—
Jesus hung willingly on a cross.
“Christ died for our sins in accordance with the Scriptures.” (1 Corinthians 15:3)
But here’s the question that won’t leave you:
Because here’s the truth most people don’t want to hear:
Delayed judgment is not canceled judgment.
And grace is not permission to stay lost.
“Or do you presume on the riches of his kindness… not knowing that God’s kindness is meant to lead you to repentance?” (Romans 2:4)
your story is not over yet.
Which means grace is still reaching.
The Father is not standing with a sword.
But the way back is not pride.
“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” (1 John 1:9)
So what are you holding onto that is not worth your soul?
What are you defending that Christ already died to free you from?
